title: Safety-first release tactics labbook (wip)
content:
Purpose:
A working labbook for pragmatic, safety-first patterns when activating canaries and A/B experiments for LLM-powered features. Focus is on cross-functional choreo (product, infra, SRE, ML quality, legal when needed). Keep this lightweight — a tactical companion rather than final playbook.

Scope and audience:
- Scope: user-facing LLM feature launches, model variant switches, routing/fallback policy rollouts (hosted + dedicated). Not: infra-only kernel upgrades unless they impact frontend latency or correctness.
- Audience: release stewards, product owners, SRE oncall, solutions eng, ML quality.

Goals:
- Minimize user-visible regressions while enabling fast iterative experiments.
- Provide crisp, executable guardrails for small-batch exposure.
- Capture fast learnings and failure-mode notes so next team avoids same pitfalls.

Non-goals:
- This is not the canonical SLA doc. Not a replacement for legal/compliance review checklist for Private customers.

Quick-start checklist (one-pager for a steward):
1) Preflight: smoke tests green, synthetic traffic profile loaded (see recipe below).
2) Metrics: baseline snapshot saved (latency P50/P95, cost/tokens, rejection rate, hallucination score).
3) Cohort: pick microcohort (<= 3% of active users OR 50 requests/min max).
4) Observability: dashboard links + pager routing verified.
5) Fallbacks: default-model fallback and region fallback enabled.
6) Roll: enable 1% -> watch 30–60m -> 5% -> 30–60m -> 20% -> hold & analyze -> proceed or revert.
7) Postmortem: capture signals and decisions even if rollout succeeds.

Signal taxonomy (how we judge safety):
- Platform signals (SRE): 5xx rate, queue length, GPU OOM events, pod restart rate.
- Latency signals: P50/P95/P99 request latency, tail knots during synthetic bursts.
- Unit-economics signals: tokens per request, cost-per-req delta vs baseline.
- Correctness signals (MLQ): hallucination proxy (QA eval on sample set), toxicity filter hits, rerank delta.
- Product/business signals: conversion or retention leading indicator, cancellation or refund spikes.
- Amplification signals: rate of cascading prompts (e.g., tool-calls spawned by model).

Threshold conventions (example, tweak per-feature):
- Immediate rollback triggers: 5xx rate > +1.0pp absolute vs baseline sustained > 5m; P95 latency increase > 200% absolute; hallucination score > 3x baseline on sampled eval.
- Escalation triggers: 5xx +0.3–1.0pp sustained 10m; tokens-per-session +30% w/o revenue uplift for 30m.
- Observation-only flags: small deviations for <30m, look for trend.

Microcohort selection heuristics:
- Start with internal-only or beta orgs when available.
- If real users: choose low-risk geography + non-critical personas (power users excluded).
- Avoid cohorts with high cost-per-conversion (e.g., paid trial customers) unless experiment purpose is revenue.
- Prefer deterministic cohorts (by account id hash) to make replay and rollback precise.

Synthetic traffic recipe (reproducible smoke):
- Profile: 60% short prompts (<=40 tokens), 30% medium (40–200), 10% long (>200).
- Burst tests: 10s ramp to 5x baseline QPS for two windows in different routes.
- Semantic sanity: include 20 prompt templates from top errors observed in last 90 days to exercise fallback, safety filters, and tool-calls.
- Recording: record a golden trace for golden-model vs canary comparison (store as artifact id).

Rollout orchestration runbook (stepwise):
- T-48h: notify cross-team stakeholders; publish canary hypothesis (what success looks like) in channel #release-orchestra and tag oncall.
- T-6h: preflight successful, capacity confirmed, synthetic traffic scripts loaded in staging.
- T-10m: enable 1% traffic slice, annotate request logs with canary-id.
- T+30m: steward reads dashboard, run sanity eval (10 random convo samples), confirm no red flags.
- If green -> accelerate to 5% then 20% with same cadence.
- If any immediate rollback trigger -> flip traffic to fallback and run postmortem.

Fallback matrix (example mapping):
- Model assertion failure -> fallback to pinned older model (same backend).
- Latency spike -> route to cheaper-latency variant (lower context-length) + notify.
- Cost runaway -> apply temporary per-customer token cap + route to quantized variant.

Human roles and responsibilities (abbreviated):
- Steward: owns hypothesis, triggers rollout, monitors for first 60m, calls rollback if thresholds hit.
- SRE oncall: monitors platform signals and executes infra mitigations (scale/policy changes).
- ML Quality: runs the adjudication checks if hallucination/toxicity flags trigger; provides quick verdict.
- Product PM: watches UX/business KPIs and decides go/no-go at larger exposures.
- Legal/Privacy: alerted for PII/loss incidents or regulated-customer impacts.

Escalation script (sample Slack + phone):
1) Steward posts in #release-orchestra: "ROLLBACK: {feature} at X% due to P95 up 250%" and tags @sre-oncall.
2) If no ack in 2 minutes, escalate to paging policy.
3) Triage call (10m standup) to decide revert vs patch.

Experiment logging and artifacts to capture:
- Baseline snapshot id (artifact), canary snapshot id.
- Synthetic trace id and replay script used.
- Sampled request/responses (redact PII).
- Decision log (who decided what and when).

Short play notes / gotchas we've hit before:
- Mirror-route asymmetry: small routing changes can add headers that change model tokenization behavior (surprising).
- Caching: prefix cache invalidation created flakiness in 1st-minute traffic; add cache-warm step in preflight.
- Metric latency: some telemetry pipelines have 2–5m ingestion lag — ensure guardrails account for ingestion delay.
- Synthetic parity: make synthetic prompts reflect actual user phrasing (we discovered a mismatch that missed hallucination bursts).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we auto-simulate cohort-specific traffic to reduce manual selection friction? (ticket: JIRA-INFR-3421)
- Should rollback triggers be standardized across teams or per-feature tuned? propose baseline + per-feature overrides.
- Need a light-weight consent flow for internal beta cohorts in region X.
- Automate golden-trace nightly replays for drift detection.

References and quick links:
- Dashboard template: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/rollout-template
- Release orchestra channel: slack://channel?team=redwood&id=release-orchestra
- Related playbook (formal): CONFLUENCE-3456
- Infra ticket for cohort simulator: JIRA-INFR-3421

Notes-to-self (informal):
- Keep this file minimal; prefer copying small fragments into feature-specific runbooks.
- After 2 successful canaries, capture a short "lessons" bullet list on the feature card.
- Remind QA to include 2 regression prompts that exercise tool-calls in any LLM feature test.

(End of labbook — will iterate with feedback from Steward rotation on Feb retrospective)
